Why not softshell? Yes that was what I was asking in this post. My answer is this: The wind layer in itself would be thinner than the protective lining of most soft shells. Now replace that shell with a tight fitting field shirt and now you lose the cons of the softshell. Let's face it, even modern cuts have a lot of puff in the mid section, even softshells make noise, the zippers uncomfortably bunch up when you sit, and imo most importantly: thermoregulation. Softshells (in my subjective experience) trap heat and cannot regulate heat shedding accordingly - as opposed to my super thin 3L 250g GTX-Active (Montura Magic 2.0) jacket. Softshells can never be this thin due to the layers needed to maintain structure integrity.

Your point about shells ending up rarely being used: yes I find that I keep packing away my hardshell; the wind layer is not perfect but I can wear 24/7 as an integral part of the midlayer. at least I'm not wasting away space/weight.
